runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets closed mostly higher Monday as Anthropic PBC's stellar revenue growth sparked a global AI re-rating wave. Japan's Nikkei 225 added 0.74% to 69,220 — within striking distance of the psychological 70,000 milestone — led by tech heavyweights and semiconductor names including Kioxia (+15%). South Korean markets were closed for a public holiday. The Hang Seng edged up modestly while China's July activity data landed in line with muted expectations: industrial output +4.8% YoY, retail sales +1.5% YoY, underscoring weak domestic demand and weighing on consumer-linked plays.

European trade opened mixed-to-higher. The DAX gained 0.53% to 26,440 on tech-sector carry-through, while the FTSE 100 dipped 0.21% to 10,750 as energy stocks gave back some of last week's gains even as Brent crude held near $88.50 — still embedding a significant geopolitical war premium (+6% last week) from the Iran supply-disruption story. The euro strengthened modestly against a broadly weak dollar, which touched a three-month low against the DXY basket.

US pre-market futures are mixed but constructive. Nasdaq-100 futures lead with a +0.5% gain on AI momentum, S&P 500 futures edge up +0.1% after posting a third consecutive weekly gain, and Dow futures slip -0.2% ahead of a pivotal retail earnings week featuring Walmart, Home Depot, and Target. The economic calendar is light Monday — NAHB housing index is the only notable release — but Fed rate-cut odds for September sit around 30% following last week's soft retail sales and weak consumer sentiment prints. VIX at 14.2 signals complacency; the main watch risk is any hawkish Fed speaker or retail earnings miss cracking consumer confidence.

ideas.catalyst: Anthropic PBC reported stellar revenue growth confirming hyperscaler AI spend is accelerating, validating NVIDIA's data center demand outlook into 2027.
ideas.thesis: NVIDIA's H200/B200 GPU order backlog remains multi-quarter, and Anthropic's results signal that frontier AI labs are still scaling compute aggressively. Morgan Stanley names NVDA a top pick; the stock's next catalyst is the GTC China event and Q3 guidance revision cycle in late August.
ideas.key_risk: Any US export control tightening on advanced chips to China could materially trim addressable market estimates.

ideas.catalyst: JPMorgan raised AMAT price target from $515 to $660, reiterating Overweight, citing accelerating WFE spend tied to AI-driven node transitions.
ideas.thesis: Applied Materials is the largest supplier of deposition and etch equipment, with direct leverage to advanced packaging and gate-all-around nodes. The AI capex wave driving HBM and CoWoS demand means fab equipment orders are inflecting upward, and AMAT's services revenue provides recurring earnings support even in softening cycles.
ideas.key_risk: Memory market oversupply or a China revenue headwind from equipment export restrictions could weigh on near-term guidance.

ideas.catalyst: Goldman Sachs named AON to its August Conviction Buy list with a $430 price target implying 21% upside, citing NFP acquisition synergies and stronger-than-consensus 2026 organic growth.
ideas.thesis: Aon's NFP integration is tracking ahead of schedule, providing cost and revenue synergies that consensus has underestimated. The insurer-as-risk-advisor model benefits from elevated corporate risk awareness (geopolitical, cyber) and supports premium pricing power well into 2027.
ideas.key_risk: Litigation or regulatory scrutiny of large-cap insurance brokerage pricing practices could cap multiple expansion.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley lists AMZN as a top pick; retail earnings week amplifies AWS cloud re-acceleration and Prime consumer resilience visibility.
ideas.thesis: Amazon sits at the intersection of AI infrastructure (AWS Trainium/Inferentia), advertising growth, and retail optionality. Any upside retail comp from Walmart this week will lift sentiment across the consumer spectrum and pull AMZN higher on sympathy.
ideas.key_risk: AWS margin deceleration or weaker-than-expected ad RPMs could disappoint the multiple if guidance is cautious.

ideas.catalyst: Brent crude holds near $88.50/bbl — up 6% last week — as Iran-related supply disruption fears keep a durable war premium embedded in energy pricing.
ideas.thesis: XLE gives broad exposure to integrated majors (XOM, CVX) and E&Ps that directly benefit from elevated oil prices. The Iran conflict shows no near-term resolution pathway, and OPEC+ has limited spare capacity to offset any supply shock.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise ceasefire or US-Iran diplomatic breakthrough could trigger a sharp $5-8/bbl oil selloff and drag XLE lower quickly.

ideas.catalyst: The US dollar touched a three-month low Monday, providing a direct tailwind to dollar-denominated gold; Fed September rate cut probability at ~30%.
ideas.thesis: A weakening dollar, elevated geopolitical risk from the Iran conflict, and expectations for eventual Fed easing combine to make gold a compelling risk-adjusted long. Central bank reserve accumulation (China, India) provides a structural bid.
ideas.key_risk: A hotter-than-expected CPI or PPI print could push rate cut odds lower and strengthen the dollar, capping gold's upside.

ideas.catalyst: Walmart reports Q2 earnings this week — the headline retail data point setting the tone for the consumer sector — benefiting from inflationary consumer trade-down.
ideas.thesis: Walmart's omnichannel business and expanding Walmart Connect advertising platform have structurally re-rated the stock. With consumer sentiment soft but still positive, Walmart's price-competitive positioning should deliver in-line to beat results.
ideas.key_risk: A significant miss on same-store sales or downside guidance could trigger a broad retail/consumer selloff.

ideas.catalyst: Morgan Stanley names ALAB a top pick in the AI semiconductor ecosystem for PCIe and CXL connectivity solutions essential for high-density AI cluster builds.
ideas.thesis: Astera Labs sits at the critical interconnect layer of AI data centers, providing PCIe retimers and CXL memory controllers that enable GPU clusters to scale. As hyperscalers expand next-gen data centers, ALAB's content-per-rack grows disproportionately.
ideas.key_risk: Customer concentration in a small number of hyperscalers and competitive pressure from Marvell custom ASICs could compress margins faster than expected.

ideas.catalyst: TTD slipped 2.5% in post-earnings trading, signaling even a solid print was not enough to satisfy elevated buy-side expectations in a richly valued digital advertising stock.
ideas.thesis: The Trade Desk trades at a significant premium to peers on assumptions of rapid CTV/programmatic share gains. When results meet but do not substantially beat, the air tends to come out of high-multiple names. The post-earnings fade pattern in TTD over the past four quarters has been consistent.
ideas.key_risk: Any acceleration in streaming ad inventory data confirming TTD's CTV thesis could trigger a sharp short squeeze.

ideas.catalyst: DA Davidson's Gil Luria downgraded BZAI from Buy to Neutral and slashed the price target from $3 to $1, citing deteriorating competitive positioning in edge AI inference.
ideas.thesis: Blaize operates in the highly competitive edge AI chip space against Qualcomm and NVIDIA's Jetson platform. With limited revenue scale, high cash burn, and analyst abandonment, the path to profitability has become materially harder. The new $1 PT implies further meaningful downside.
ideas.key_risk: A surprise OEM partnership announcement could temporarily reverse the downward trend despite weak fundamentals.

deals.headline: Nielsen to Acquire DoubleVerify for $2.15 Billion
deals.description: Nielsen announced an all-cash agreement to acquire digital ad measurement firm DoubleVerify for $2.15 billion, expanding its digital advertising verification and media intelligence capabilities. The deal combines Nielsen's legacy media ratings business with DoubleVerify's programmatic ad fraud detection and brand safety tools.
deals.impact: High — consolidates digital ad measurement landscape; DV shareholders receive significant premium
deals.sentiment: Bullish for DV; Neutral-Cautious for NLSN

deals.headline: Teledyne Technologies to Acquire Varex Imaging for $1.1 Billion
deals.description: Teledyne Technologies agreed to acquire Varex Imaging, a maker of X-ray imaging components and detection systems, for $1.1 billion. The acquisition expands Teledyne's medical imaging and industrial inspection product lines with recurring revenue from healthcare and security screening contracts.
deals.impact: Moderate — Teledyne gains medical imaging scale; Varex shareholders receive strategic premium
deals.sentiment: Bullish for VREX; Neutral for TDY

deals.headline: Dream Finders Homes to Acquire Beazer Homes for $915 Million
deals.description: Dream Finders Homes announced a definitive agreement to acquire Beazer Homes USA for $915 million, creating a top-10 US homebuilder by community count. The deal accelerates Dream Finders' Southeast and Mid-Atlantic market penetration while gaining Beazer's mortgage origination platform.
deals.impact: High — creates meaningful scale in homebuilding; BZH receives premium
deals.sentiment: Bullish for BZH; Mixed for DFH (integration risk)

deals.headline: OpenAI Acquires Presentation AI Startup NextSlide
deals.description: OpenAI confirmed the acquisition of NextSlide, an AI-powered presentation and slide generation startup, to embed AI productivity tools into enterprise workflows beyond chat interfaces. The deal accelerates OpenAI's enterprise product suite to compete with Microsoft Copilot's presentation capabilities.
deals.impact: Moderate — OpenAI (private) expands enterprise AI; Microsoft competitive read-through
deals.sentiment: Slightly Bearish for MSFT (increased OpenAI enterprise competition)

deals.headline: Goldman Sachs Adds AON to August Conviction Buy List with $430 Price Target
deals.description: Goldman Sachs added Aon plc to its August Conviction Buy List with a $430 price target implying approximately 21% upside. Analyst Rob Cox highlighted stronger-than-consensus 2026 organic growth from NFP acquisition synergies and attractive free cash flow yield as the primary drivers.
deals.impact: High — Goldman conviction list placement historically drives institutional buying flow
